A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPRINT study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, architectural ablations, representation analyses, and training-speed and memory measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds controlled MDTv2 comparisons, scheduled-guidance results, and a fine-tuning-duration study.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 3 add an optional guidance-scheduled PDG inference variant. The core SPRINT architecture, residual fusion, structured token sampling, training losses, and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K class-conditional generation at 256×256 and 512×512, retaining the same SD/Flux latent coverage. The added baseline, guidance, and fine-tuning experiments introduce no new dataset, domain, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 newly includes MDTv2 in the controlled SD-autoencoder comparisons at 400K and 1M iterations. MDTv2 already appeared in v1's broader Table 3 comparison, but its participation in this controlled experiment is new. Other comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the stated 512×512 PDG guidance scales from 1.25/1.5 for FID/FDD to 1.35/1.8. New evaluations add guidance scheduling and a sweep of fine-tuning durations through 200K steps after 2M pretraining iterations. These are limited protocol extensions and revisions; the PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4.5 and Figures 8–9 test how fine-tuning duration affects visual details and FID under CFG and PDG. Table 3 also permits comparison with and without guidance scheduling. Existing path, depth, drop-ratio, representation, and few-step analyses remain.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MDTv2 scores. Table 3 adds unscheduled MDTv2 and scheduled-PDG results, including FID 1.55 without REPA and 1.49 with REPA, fills comparator compute values, and removes the 200-epoch improved-SiT and non-REPA SPRINT-PDG entries. Table 10 replaces PDG FID 2.55 with 1.96 and precision/recall 0.84/0.55 with 0.83/0.58 alongside revised guidance scales, so this is not a same-setting gain. Figures 8–9 add fine-tuning findings; most existing results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flow-matching objective, token-sampling formula, and guidance equations are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: effective 75% token dropping, up to 9.8× training savings, approximately halved guidance inference cost, and compatibility across architectures and latent spaces. The added introductory PDG paragraph explains an existing contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly interprets fine-tuning as recovering high-frequency details, with most benefit obtained within 20K–50K steps and limited sensitivity to longer fine-tuning. Section 4.4 expands the explanation for dense encoder and decoder processing. Appendix H's applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and revises the documented 512×512 guidance scales in Appendix C.2. Most implementation details, hardware specifications, and hyperparameters are retained. The reproducibility statement still says training code cannot be released at submission, so the link alone does not establish code availability.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, including Kynkäänniemi et al. (2024) for guidance scheduling and additional PCA, training, and evaluation references. The main related-work discussion and positioning against token-dropping and representation-alignment methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an introductory PDG explanation and Section 4.5, expands the depth-ablation discussion, and makes localized wording and caption edits. The overall narrative and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 8–9, includes MDTv2 in Figure 1, expands and reorganizes Tables 1 and 3, swaps Tables 4–5, and adjusts several figure labels, sizes, and placements. Citation coloring and page flow change. Existing appendix image panels are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The controlled MDTv2 comparisons and fine-tuning-duration study provide more direct support for aggressive token dropping and rapid adaptation to full-token inference. These focused additions modestly strengthen the paper. Benefits are tempered by removed 200-epoch comparisons, underspecified guidance scheduling, and reporting inconsistencies, including v2's baseline FID of 2.63 in the higher-resolution discussion versus 2.62 in Table 10.
